Listen to this article Share THE NIGERIAN National Petroleum Company (NNPC) Limited is set to commence the construction of a proposed 10,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) condensate refinery in Edo State following the presentation of a Certificate of Occupancy (C-of-O) by the state government. Advertisement Advertisement The proposed refinery, known as Oredo Refinery and Petrochemical Company Limited, is located in Ologbo, Ikpoba-Okha Local Government Area of the state. Mumuni Dagazau, Executive Vice President, Downstream, NNPC Limited, led a delegation of the company and its partners to Benin City to receive the certificate from Monday Okpebholo, governor of Edo State. Speaking during the presentation, Okpebholo commended the management of NNPCL and its partners for choosing Edo State for the investment, describing the project as an important opportunity to boost the state’s economic development. Okpebholo said the refinery would expand the state’s commercial base, create employment opportunities for residents and increase its internally generated revenue. “I’m delighted to present to you the certificate of occupancy, just as I promised you that I’m going to give you my support by giving you land to invest in Edo State because the investment is so dear to us in Edo State. Advertisement “It will give us more revenue and our people will also be employed. It is going to expand our commercial base in Edo State, and I believe that Edo people will openly receive the investment,” he said. In his remarks, Dagazau thanked the governor for fulfilling his commitment to facilitate the land requirements and documentation for the project. Advertisement He said the Federal Government, under the leadership of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, had renewed its focus on strengthening Nigeria’s domestic refining capacity, improving energy security, reducing dependence on imported petroleum products and maximising value from the country’s hydrocarbon resources. According to him, the project aligns with the President’s Renewed Hope Agenda, which seeks to move Nigeria from dependence on imported refined petroleum products towards greater domestic processing, value addition, industrial growth and economic resilience. Advertisement Advertisement Dagazau said NNPCL, under the leadership of its Group Chief Executive Officer, Bashir Bayo Ojulari, was translating these national objectives into commercially sustainable investment opportunities through strategic partnerships, disciplined capital deployment and operational efficiency. “The proposed 10,000-barrel-per-day Oredo Condensate Refinery is an important expression of this strategy. It represents an opportunity to expand domestic processing capacity, improve the availability of refined petroleum products within the region and strengthen the downstream petroleum value chain,” he added. He also added that the project would also provide employment opportunities, promote technology transfer, encourage local enterprise participation and stimulate supporting industrial and commercial activities. The NNPCL executive particularly commended the Edo State Government for participating in the project not only as a facilitator of the investment but also as a shareholder and development partner. “This alignment of government support, investment capital and commercial expertise provides a strong foundation for a successful project,” he stated. Dagazau described the Certificate of Occupancy as more than a legal document, noting that it was a critical enabler of investment and another step towards translating the refinery project into physical infrastructure and productive economic activity. He said NNPCL would work closely with its partners to address the technical, commercial, regulatory and financing requirements necessary to bring the project to fruition. He added that the company looks forward to delivering a refinery that would serve Edo State, contribute to Nigeria’s energy security and demonstrate the benefits of purposeful collaboration between government and private sector investors. He further explained that the refinery would process condensate, a very light liquid hydrocarbon produced alongside natural gas. The proposed 10,000bpd facility is expected to strengthen domestic refining capacity and deepen economic activities within Edo State and the wider region.
